Program 1: Browser-Based Pet Care Appointment Interface

Course Outcomes: CO1 (HTML/CSS & DOM manipulation) and CO2 (Asynchronous JavaScript & Fetch API)

1. Aim & Objectives

To design and implement a responsive browser-based pet care appointment interface using semantic HTML5, CSS3, and modern vanilla JavaScript. The interface validates user inputs, demonstrates asynchronous data retrieval using Fetch API with async/await, dynamically updates the DOM, supports multi-field sorting, and logs simulated HTTP network operations in real time.

2. Theoretical Highlights

  • DOM Event Handling: Event listeners intercept input, change, and submit actions, executing validation without page refreshes.
  • Fetch API with async/await: Native Promise-based HTTP requests fetch remote datasets cleanly and handle network errors gracefully.
  • JSON Data Interchange: Form input is converted to standard JSON request payloads and rendered dynamically onto the view.
Figure 1.1: Program 1 Main Dashboard View showing KPI metrics, appointment booking form, appointment cards, and live HTTP activity inspector.
Figure 1.2: Program 1 Dynamic Form Submission and Modal Dialog for editing consultation status and doctor's clinical notes.

Program 2: React Application for Pet Care Appointment

Course Outcome: CO3 (React Functional Components, JSX, Props, State, Hooks & Routing)

1. Aim & Objectives

To architect a Single-Page Application (SPA) in React 18 for pet care appointment booking. Demonstrates modular functional components, JSX, props and state management via useState and useEffect, conditional rendering, and client-side routing with React Router DOM v6.

2. Theoretical Highlights

  • Component-Driven Architecture: UI is partitioned into reusable components (Navbar, AppointmentCard, AppointmentForm, StatsSummary).
  • React Hooks: useState manages local form state; useEffect synchronizes state with browser localStorage.
  • React Router v6: Declarative routing between listing view (/), booking form (/book), and operational analytics (/analytics).
Figure 2.1: React Application Home View displaying appointment cards, search and filter controls, and dynamic KPI statistics.
Figure 2.2: React Controlled Booking Form Component with input validation and state management.
Figure 2.3: React Operational Analytics View displaying service distribution and species breakdown.

Program 3: Node.js Server-Side Utility without Express

Course Outcome: CO4 (Node.js Core Modules: HTTP, File System, Path, Events, and Streams)

1. Aim & Objectives

To develop a server-side pet care appointment utility purely with native Node.js core modules. Implements an HTTP server using http.createServer, stores and retrieves JSON records using fs.promises and path, dispatches lifecycle events with EventEmitter, and streams CSV data with stream.Readable.

2. Theoretical Highlights

  • Native HTTP Server: Implements manual request routing for GET, POST, PUT, DELETE without external frameworks.
  • Asynchronous File I/O: Reads and writes records from flat files non-blockingly using fs.promises.
  • EventEmitter: Decoupled notification dispatching (appointment:created, appointment:updated, appointment:cancelled).
  • Node.js Streams: Memory-efficient CSV export using stream.Readable.pipe(res) and log streaming via fs.createReadStream.
Figure 3.1: Program 3 Core Node.js HTTP Server Web Dashboard and Route Catalog.
Figure 3.2: Program 3 API Appointments JSON Response loaded asynchronously from file storage.

Program 4: Express.js REST API with Middleware & JWT Security

Course Outcome: CO5 (RESTful APIs, Custom Middleware, Centralized Error Handling, JWT & Bcrypt)

1. Aim & Objectives

To develop a full-featured Express.js REST API for pet care appointment management. Features complete CRUD routes, custom request logging, input validation middleware, centralized error handling, and role-protected routes secured with bcrypt password hashing and signed JWT tokens.

2. Theoretical Highlights

  • Middleware Pipeline: Middleware sequence handles latency logging, CORS, body parsing, input validation, and JWT verification.
  • Bcrypt Password Hashing: Applies 10 salt rounds to hash credentials, protecting against rainbow table attacks.
  • JWT Authentication: Issues signed bearer tokens verifying authenticity without server session storage.
  • Centralized Error Handling: Catches operational and runtime errors, responding with standardized JSON status codes.
Figure 4.1: Express REST API Documentation Dashboard displaying route manifest and authentication rules.
Figure 4.2: Express REST API Appointments Endpoint delivering filtered JSON records.

Program 5: Full-Stack Integration & Cloud Deployment

Course Outcome: CO6 (Full-Stack Architecture, Sequelize ORM, CORS, Environment Variables & Cloud Deployment)

1. Aim & Objectives

To integrate the React frontend with an Express backend, persisting data using Sequelize ORM with PostgreSQL and SQLite support. Implements CORS, environment variable isolation, and cloud deployment configuration for Vercel (frontend) and Render (backend).

2. Theoretical Highlights

  • Full-Stack Architecture: Decoupled React client communicating with Express REST API over HTTP/JSON.
  • Sequelize ORM: Maps JavaScript models (User, Appointment) to SQL tables with schema migrations and validation.
  • CORS & Environment Variables: Configures cross-origin access and separates configuration via .env.
  • Cloud Deployment: Automated build manifests for Vercel (vercel.json) and Render (render.yaml).
